title: Dispatch: Persist campaign rules in canonical campaign history (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 1). Spec and acceptance criteria live on eshyra-jhpt.2 and the epic eshyra-jhpt; read both. This bead carries the supervisor's pre-planning only.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.1, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (merge dee4471, which already contains the completed eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model). Work only inside that worktree.

SCOPE
Durable storage + query APIs only. NO prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), NO ambiguity dialogue (.6), NO replay orchestration (.8), NO CLI (.5). Build on the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model in packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts — do not redefine its types, re-derive its ordering, or fork its validation.

CODE SURVEY (verified against dee4471)

1. THE DOMAIN MODEL YOU BUILD ON (packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts, exported via src/internal.ts).
   CampaignRule { ruleIdentity, campaignId, ruleKind: 'ruling'|'house-rule', status: 'active'|'revoked'|'superseded', origin: 'player-authored'|'player-approved'|'oracle-supplied', provenance (discriminated: 'ambiguity' {ambiguityId, selectedInterpretationId} | 'recurring-question' {questionId} | 'house-rule' {rationale?}), effectivePosition: CampaignPosition, temporalMode ('prospective' | 'disputed-turn' {disputedPosition}), supersededBy: string|null, scope, governingRecordKeys, prose }.
   CampaignPosition { sessionId, turnId, ordinal }. formatCampaignPosition emits `cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~<encoded session>~<encoded turn>`, which is CANONICAL AND SELF-SORTING: byte order equals chronological order. That property was added deliberately (eshyra-jhpt.1.3) so that SQL `ORDER BY effective_position` and `WHERE effective_position <= ?` are correct WITHOUT parsing. Store the canonical string in a TEXT column and rely on it; do not store a separate ordinal integer as the sort key and do not sort in JS after a full table scan. Use validateCampaignRule / validateCampaignRules on write and projectCampaignRule for the read projection.

2. THE READ SEAM YOU MUST IMPLEMENT IS ALREADY SPECIFIED AND ALREADY CONSUMED ON MAIN.
   packages/core/src/discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts consumes CampaignRuleReadSeam (declared in discovery/types.ts, projection types re-exported from the campaign domain). eshyra-jhpt.3's amendment A1 and the transition's W11 depend on this being the ONE campaign-rule read interface; a discovery-local store is explicitly forbidden.
   THE EXACT CONTRACT IS PINNED BY AN IN-REPO REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION: packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts. Read it before you design the queries. It establishes, and your DB-backed implementation must match:
     - activeRulesAtPosition returns HOUSE RULES ONLY (the oracle filters ruleKind === 'house-rule'). Rulings are NOT returned here; they are returned only by activeRulingsForAmbiguities. campaignRuleSeam.ts concatenates the two results (`[...rules, ...rulings]`), so returning rulings from both would double-process them.
     - candidateRecordKeys is a HINT, NOT A FILTER. The oracle ignores it and returns every active house rule. campaignRuleSeam.ts's own comment is explicit: "R1 is about active rules applicable to the situation, not about whether discovery already found candidates, so a rule can surface governing material even when nothing else did." A rule whose governing keys are not among the candidates must still be RETURNED — the seam then either surfaces its governing record as a new candidate or records it as an `unplaced-rule` loss. If you filter by candidateRecordKeys you will silently break that route and the loss accounting.
     - activeRulingsForAmbiguities(ids) returns active rulings whose ambiguityId is in ids.
   Only an 'ambiguity'-provenance ruling may be projected as a CampaignRulingProjection (eshyra-jhpt.1.2 fixed a fabrication defect here). Note eshyra-neus tracks the discovery-side cast that is unsound for recurring-question rulings — do NOT fix that here; it is discovery's, not storage's.

3. MIGRATIONS ARE THE ONLY SCHEMA AUTHORITY (ADR 0015). Add the next migration under packages/core/data/migrations/ (highest today is 0024_active_effect_zone_form_projections.sql, so yours is 0025_*.sql). There is no hand-maintained latest-schema DDL and no CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repair path; migrationRunner.ts verifies checksums of applied migrations, so never edit a migration that already exists. Follow the style of 0024: explicit CHECK constraints on every closed enum, named indexes, PRIMARY KEY on (campaign_id, ...). Mirror the domain's closed unions as CHECK constraints so the DB rejects what the domain rejects. Check whether packages/core/data/schema.snapshot.sql is generated or hand-maintained and update it the way the repo expects.

4. CHECKPOINT/RESTORE IS AUTOMATIC — DO NOT BUILD A MECHANISM. packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts enumerates tables from sqlite_master ("SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'") and snapshots every one. A new table is therefore included for free. What you owe is a TEST proving the round trip preserves identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions, per the acceptance criteria — not new checkpoint code.

5. CAMPAIGN SCOPE. A campaign DB is single-campaign (campaign.ts stores campaign_id in meta), but the acceptance criteria still require cross-campaign isolation and rejection of cross-campaign supersession. Carry campaign_id on the table and enforce it in queries and in validation, matching validateCampaignRules which already rejects supersession across campaigns.

DESIGN NOTES / JUDGMENT CALLS

- REVOCATION NEEDS ITS OWN POSITION COLUMN. The domain has status 'revoked' but no revocation position; the epic requires revocation to be prospective and requires active-at-position queries to be correct for a position BEFORE a later revocation. Add a revoked-at-position column (nullable, canonical position string) so "active at position P" is: status not superseded, effective_position <= P, and (revoked_position IS NULL OR revoked_position > P). Report in your notes that this field is storage-side state the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain type does not carry, and say whether you think the domain type should gain it — if you believe it should, file a bd issue rather than editing the domain model here.
- SUPERSESSION likewise: a superseded rule must stop being active from the successor's effective position, not retroactively. Make sure your active-at-position predicate gets that right and test it at a position before and after the supersession.
- Persist provenance losslessly. The projection's `provenance` is a flattened display string; the discriminated union is the real data. Store the discriminant plus its fields in typed columns (or one JSON column via persistence/jsonColumn.ts, which is the established idiom — see rules/binding.ts addonsColumn) so a round trip reconstructs the exact CampaignRule, not just its projection.
- governingRecordKeys is a string array: use jsonColumn, consistent with the rest of the codebase.

REQUIRED OUTPUTS
- Migration 0025 creating the campaign-rule table with CHECK-constrained enums and the indexes the queries need.
- A storage module (suggested packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRuleStore.ts) with create, read-by-identity, list, supersede, revoke, and active-at-position query APIs, all campaign-scoped and deterministically ordered.
- A DB-backed CampaignRuleReadSeam implementation matching the oracle contract in point 2 exactly.
- Exports added to packages/core/src/internal.ts (NOT index.ts — new core symbols default to internal per AGENTS.md § Conventions).
- Tests: create/read/list/supersede/revoke; active-at-position determinism including a position before and after both a supersession and a revocation; prospective vs disputed-turn effective positions; invalid cross-campaign and invalid supersession combinations; checkpoint/restore round trip; and a test asserting the seam implementation matches the oracle contract (house-rules-only from activeRulesAtPosition, candidateRecordKeys not used as a filter, rulings only via activeRulingsForAmbiguities).

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
